correctness.rationale: The hazard transform makes all edge clocks iid Exp(1). For any prescribed matching, exactly k(2n-2k-1) incident clocks must exceed t; after memorylessness the known reciprocal matching product yields the exact all-order threshold formula. For r isolated vertices, rn-r(r+1)/2 is the exact number of distinct clocks forced above u. At t=(log(n(n-1)/(2(2n-3)))+y)/(2n-3) and u=(log n+x)/n both one-type factorial moments converge to Poisson means. Conditional on a fixed disjoint set of isolated vertices, the remaining graph has unchanged independent clocks; conditional reciprocal matching edge arrivals have sequential Exp(j(2m-2j-1)) increments, expected last excess O(1/n), hence chance of passing the higher u threshold is O(1/log n). Overlapping configurations contribute o(1) using their forced high pair time and independent unaffected isolation edges. All mixed factorial moments factor, and the independent bivariate Poisson limit gives independent Gumbels. Exhaustive edge-rank cases n<=4 and 4123 deterministic checks passed from actual VERIFY.py; those are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: In a symmetric random-link nearest-neighbor network the last vertex to acquire any adjacent edge and the last reciprocally nearest pair have distinct, naturally observable extreme thresholds, with leading exponential-hazard scales log(n)/n and log(n)/(2n). Their limiting independence supplies valid simultaneous tail calibration despite shared edge data, beyond either marginal extreme-value theorem. The pair clock also has a direct interpretation as the last edge joining two isolated vertices in the increasing random graph process. This is a motivated rare-event network property, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
